confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for prices. Food and drink anchors come from aggregated cost-of-living guides (traveltables, mylifeelsewhere, oysterlist and similar), which are crowdsourced and often undated or from about 2023. They disagree: domestic beer ranged from about $1.4 to $3.1, an inexpensive meal from about $4 to $8, and a mid-range meal for two was about $19-20. Resort and Naama Bay venues cost more than Old Market cafes, so I set beer, meal and coffee anchors slightly above the cheapest figures. One guide gave Naama Bay bar prices of EGP 80-180 for local beer and EGP 200-400 for cocktails. I found no direct cocktail or wine-by-the-glass price for Sharm. I estimated cocktail from that guide's cocktail range, and wine from the local beer price (roughly 2x beer, local Egyptian wine). Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, with no booking pages or listings searched. Registered hostel supply in Sharm is thin, so the hostel anchors are the least certain. July is hot, and prices can vary by season and by all-inclusive packaging. The RBA figure comes from a search result summarising the RBA exchange-rates page, which gave AUD/USD of 0.6720 at 4.00 pm on 18 November 2026. I did not open the RBA page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Sharm El Sheikh is a tourist-oriented Red Sea resort. Sources put its restaurant prices near Hurghada's and below Cairo hotel-bar levels. I took Hurghada and Egyptian Red Sea resort pricing as the basis, with a modest tourist-area premium over local Old Market prices.
